video_caption: The video opens with a person speaking, while on screen, a Windows desktop is visible, displaying an open "This PC" (file explorer) window. The desktop background features a stunning aerial view of a winding road cutting through lush green mountains, with blurred light trails suggesting rapid movement or a long-exposure photograph. The "This PC" window shows common folders like "Desktop," "Documents," "Downloads," "Music," "Pictures," and "Videos." Below these, various "Devices and drives" are listed, including "Windows (C:)" with "639 GB free of 1.34 TB," "RECOVERY (D:)" with "2.28 GB free of 20.5 GB," "DVD RW Drive (E:)," "CD Drive (F:)," "CD Drive (G:)," and a highlighted "USB Drive (I:)" showing "13.2 GB free of 14.7 GB." Under "Network locations (3)," "AKHCustom," "kadersh@hotmail.com (akh)," and "osmsc" are listed. The person is discussing how to install Kodi to a USB drive, making it portable. The taskbar at the bottom of the screen contains various application icons, a search bar labeled "Ask me anything," and the current time and date "18:46" and "27/09/2016." The "This PC" window remains the main focus as the speaker elaborates on the utility of a portable Kodi installation for use at work, school, or with friends.

The video segment displays a Windows desktop environment with a "Kodi Setup" installation window open in the foreground. The background is a blurred image of a highway at night, showing streaks of car lights. The "Kodi Setup" window features the Kodi logo and the title "Installing," with the message "Please wait while Kodi is being installed." A progress bar shows the extraction of various files, starting with "Extract: Kodi.exe... 11%" and progressively reaching higher percentages, then continuing with files like `d3dcompiler_47.dll`, `iconv.dll`, `libxml2.dll`, `python27.dll`, `python27.pdb`, `addon.xml`, `libXBMC_pvr.dll`, and `strings.po`, each file extraction completing at 100% before moving to the next. The installation process is indicated by the changing filenames and advancing progress bar. At the bottom of the window, "Nullsoft Install System v2.50" is visible, along with disabled navigation buttons "< Back" and "Next >", and an enabled "Cancel" button. Around the 0:21 mark, the installation completes, and the window changes to "Completing the Kodi Setup Wizard," stating "Kodi has been installed on your computer. Click Finish to close this wizard." A checkbox labeled "Run Kodi" is present but unchecked, and a link "Please visit http://kodi.tv for more information" is displayed. A "ding" sound is heard, and the mouse cursor moves and clicks the now-enabled "Finish" button, signifying the conclusion of the setup.

The video segment opens with a "Completing the Kodi Setup Wizard" window on a Windows desktop. The text reads, "Kodi has been installed on your computer. Click Finish to close this wizard." Below this is an unchecked checkbox labeled "Run Kodi" and a link "Please visit http://kodi.tv for more information." The user clicks the "Finish" button. The wizard closes, revealing a File Explorer window titled "Kodi Build" open to "This PC > Desktop > Kodi Build". The selected item is "kodi-16.1-Jarvis.exe" (an application). On the left pane, the user navigates down to "USB Drive (L:)" and clicks it. The File Explorer then shows the contents of "USB Drive (L:)", which contains a single folder named "Kodi". The user opens the "Kodi" folder, displaying several files and folders, including "addons", "media", "system", "userdata", and multiple .dll files, as well as "Kodi.exe" (an application, 20,363 KB). The user then right-clicks on the empty space within the File Explorer window, opening a context menu with options like "View", "Sort by", "Refresh", "Paste", "Paste shortcut", "Undo Delete Ctrl+Z", "New", "Display settings", and "Personalise". The user hovers over "New", which expands to a sub-menu, and clicks on "Shortcut". This action brings up a "Create Shortcut" wizard window with the title "Create Shortcut" and the text, "This wizard helps you to create shortcuts to local or network programs, files, folders, computers or Internet addresses." Below, there's a text input field labeled "Type the location of the item:" and a "Browse..." button next to it, with "Next" and "Cancel" buttons at the bottom.

The video segment shows a computer screen displaying an open "Create Shortcut" wizard. Initially, a dialog box titled "Select the target of the shortcut below:" is visible, showing a file explorer structure. The user navigates by expanding "USB Drive (I:)" and then the "Kodi" folder, which contains several subfolders like "addons," "media," "system," and "userdata," along with various files. The user selects "Kodi.exe," and a tooltip briefly appears, showing its details as "Type: Application," "Size: 19.8 MB," and "Date modified: 24/04/2016 10:30." After clicking "OK," the dialog transitions to "What item would you like to create a shortcut for?" where the field "Type the location of the item:" is pre-filled with "I:\Kodi\Kodi.exe." The user then types " -p" after the existing text in the location field before clicking the "Next" button. The wizard then shows the "What would you like to name the shortcut?" prompt, with "Kodi.exe" already in the "Type a name for this shortcut:" field. The user clicks "Finish" to complete the process. The background of the screen appears to be a desktop wallpaper featuring abstract, colorful lines.

The video segment opens with a view of a computer screen, split between a Windows file explorer window on the left and a desktop background depicting a winding road through a lush, green landscape with blurred streaks of light, suggesting vehicle motion. On the desktop, a mouse cursor hovers over a shortcut icon labeled "Kodi.exe" (Kodi.exe), featuring a blue "K" logo. The file explorer window displays the contents of a folder titled "Kodi" (Kodi) within "USB Drive (D:)" (USB Drive (D:)), showing multiple files (including .dll, .exe) and folders (e.g., "addons," "media," "userdata"). As the narrator explains how to create a portable version of the executable, the mouse cursor moves to and clicks the "Kodi.exe" icon on the desktop. Immediately after the click, a new folder named "portable_data" (portable_data) appears at the bottom of the file list in the open file explorer window. The screen then transitions to a full-screen display of the KODI application's splash screen, featuring the central "KODI" (KODI) logo with "v16.1 - Jarvis" (v16.1 - Jarvis) beneath it. The background is a dark blue with intricate light blue geometric shapes and lines, resembling a circuit board, with labels such as "PICTURES" (PICTURES), "VIDEOS" (VIDEOS), and "MUSIC" (MUSIC) positioned around the central logo.

The video segment opens at 00:04 on a digital interface, likely Kodi, displaying a dark blue background with abstract, out-of-focus light blue circles. In the top left corner, the "KODI" logo is visible, while the top right corner shows "6:55 PM" and "Tuesday, September 27, 2016". A horizontal navigation bar spans the middle of the screen with options like "TURES", "VIDEOS", "MUSIC", "PROGRAMS", and "SYSTE", with "MUSIC" currently highlighted, and "Files" and "Add-ons" appearing as sub-options below it. At the bottom, a darker bar contains a star icon, a power icon, and text that reads "Kodi: Kodi goes Windows Store - Kodi v17 "Krypton"". At 00:06, a dark grey pop-up menu appears in the center of the screen, offering system power options including "Exit", "Power off system", "Custom shutdown timer", "Suspend", "Hibernate", and "Reboot", with "Exit" highlighted in blue as the active selection, before the scene transitions to a desktop view at 00:09.

In this video segment, a Windows File Explorer window is open, initially displaying the contents of "This PC > USB Drive (L:) > Kodi > portable_data," which includes folders such as "addons," "cache," "media," "system," "userdata," and a "kodi.log" file. The speaker refers to putting something into this "portable_data" folder. The left sidebar shows various navigation links, and the speaker scrolls down to "Kodi Build," which they click. This action changes the main pane to show files and folders related to "Kodi Build," including executable files like "kodi-17.0-Krypton_beta2.exe" and "kodi-16.1-Jarvis.exe," as well as a "WinRAR ZIP archive" named "AKHBuild120316.zip" with a tooltip indicating its creation date and size. The view then returns to the "portable_data" folder. The speaker right-clicks within this folder and selects "Open in new window" from the context menu to create a second File Explorer window. Both windows are arranged side-by-side. In the first window (left), the speaker selects all items within "portable_data" and proceeds to delete them, as shown by a "Deleting 31 items from portable_data" progress bar that quickly reaches 99% and then 100% complete. The "portable_data" folder is now empty, displaying "This folder is empty." In the second window (right), the speaker navigates through "Kodi Build" and then into "Review Template" to a "Fresh Copy" folder. They then select the "addons" and "userdata" folders from "Fresh Copy" and drag them into the now-empty "portable_data" folder in the first window. A new progress bar appears, labeled "Copying 730 items from Fresh Copy to portable_data," which shows the copying process progressing from 4% to 38% completion by the end of the segment.

The video segment opens with a desktop displaying a scenic wallpaper of a winding mountain road at dusk, adorned with various application icons. A Windows File Explorer window is open on the left, showing the path "This PC > USB Drive (I:) > Kodi > portable_data" in its address bar, with "userdata" and "addons" listed as folders within the main panel. Simultaneously, a smaller pop-up window in the center-right indicates a file transfer in progress. This window shows "43% complete," stating "Copying 730 items from Fresh Copy to portable_data." As the video progresses, the percentage complete in the file transfer window steadily increases, moving from 43% to 62% by the end of the segment, with a green progress bar visually filling up to match the percentage. The speaker's mouse cursor, a blue circle, is visible moving around the bottom left of the screen during this time.

The video starts with a computer desktop featuring a scenic wallpaper of a winding road through mountains at dusk, displaying numerous application icons and a taskbar showing the time "19:01" and date "27/09/2016". The mouse cursor, shaped like a hand, is initially positioned over a "Kodi.exe" desktop icon. A File Explorer window opens, showing "Quick access" and a list of folders. The user navigates through the file system, eventually clicking on "USB Drive (B:)" and then into a "Kodi" folder, followed by a "portable_data" subfolder. Within this subfolder, the user right-clicks and pastes a shortcut named "Kodi.exe" (dated "27/09/2016 18:54"). After confirming the paste, the user copies this new "Kodi.exe" shortcut from the File Explorer and pastes it directly onto the desktop. The video then transitions to the Kodi application launching, displaying a dark loading screen with the blue KODI logo and the text "KODI v16.1 - Jarvis". Finally, the Kodi interface appears, showing a YouTube channel ("Game of Ohms") as its background, with navigation options "VIDEOS", "PROGRAMS", and "SYSTEM" at the bottom, and the current time "7:02 PM" and date "Tuesday, September 27, 2016" in the top right corner.

The video segment displays a static screen recording of what appears to be a Kodi media center interface, with a dominant blue and gray color scheme. At the top right, the time "7:02 PM" and date "Tuesday, September 27, 2016" are visible. Below this, a header with a bright, fiery yellow-orange abstract image is present, with the text "Game of Ohms" below it. A horizontal dark gray navigation bar prominently features "VIDEOS," "PROGRAMS," and "SYSTEM" in white text, with "VIDEOS" highlighted. Below this bar, the screen is filled with content resembling a YouTube channel. On the left, a list of "Sky Sports" channels is shown (e.g., "Sky Sports 1," "Sky Sports 2," "Sky Sports HD," "Sky Sports 4"). To the right, a section titled "DC SPORTS NEW UPDATE KODI ADDON LIVE SPORTS CHANNELS AND EVENTS" provides details and instructions for a sports add-on. Further down, several video thumbnails are displayed under a "Tutorials" section, with titles such as "How to Have Multiple Builds in Kodi," "The New Spartan Build," and "Duggan All Rounder Build Kodi 16." At the very bottom of the screen, a dark gray bar features a star icon and a power icon on the left, and continuously scrolling text in the center which reads: "Game of Ohms. EVOLVE IS BACK AND BETTER THAN EVER. Evolve is back and available in their dedicated own repo http://www.matsbuilds.co.uk/goliath/ MONEYSPORTS 4.0.3 ON KOD." No people are visible in the segment.
